item.title: We're getting ready for Google I/O 2026, and we want you to help us kick off the show. 🪄 This year, we're building a community-driven countdown for...
item.description:
We're getting ready for Google I/O 2026, and we want you to help us kick off the show. 🪄
This year, we're building a community-driven countdown for the main stage — featuring vibe coded numbers created by YOU.
We're challenging you to use Gemini Canvas or Google AI Studio to vibe code a unique app that features the numbers 1-10. No need to be a professional developer to join in — you can vibe code your idea to life just by describing your vision.
The most interesting creations will be featured on the big screen at Google I/O 2026! For more info and to submit your creation, head here → goo.gle/codethecountdown

item.title: Earlier this week, Sundar Pichai shared Q1 highlights across our AI products including the Gemini app, our developer offerings and Waymo. Beyond the t...
item.description:
Earlier this week, Sundar Pichai shared Q1 highlights across our AI products including the Gemini app, our developer offerings and Waymo. Beyond the topline numbers, here are some highlights showing our AI progress:
🍌 Nano Banana 2 hit a massive milestone: 1 billion images generated. Our latest image model achieved this in nearly half the time it took Nano Banana 1.
🎸 Since launching in the Gemini app, Lyria 3 has generated more than 150 million songs.
💻 Gemma 4, which we released just a few weeks ago, has been downloaded over 50 million times. In fact, our open models have now been downloaded over 500 million times.
👏 Q1 was our strongest subscription quarter ever for our consumer AI plans — with overall paid subscriptions reaching 350 million, including YouTube.
🚙 Waymo surpassed 500,000 fully autonomous rides per week, doubling in less than a year.
With so many opportunities ahead, we’re not slowing down anytime soon. See you at I/O on May 19 and catch up on Sundar’s full remarks from our Q1 earnings call ⬇️ https://goo.gle/4cPFEDW

item.title: What did science look like in the 18th century? 🔬 To find out, The Royal Society and Google Arts & Culture have collaborated to bring Benjamin Fran...
item.description:
What did science look like in the 18th century? 🔬
To find out, The Royal Society and Google Arts & Culture have collaborated to bring Benjamin Franklin’s original manuscripts to NotebookLM, our AI-powered research tool that helps you get a deeper understanding of any topic.
Building on a 10-year partnership, this new project uses AI to make complex, 18th-century documents machine-readable. Instead of just reading history, NotebookLM allows you to engage directly with Franklin's legacy. You can use the "Chat" panel to ask questions about the invention of the lightning rod, listen to a podcast-style Audio Overview, or test your knowledge with a custom quiz.
Check out the video to see how NotebookLM can contextualize these incredible historical sources.
Ready to dive into the archives? Explore "The Science of Benjamin Franklin" →  goo.gle/franklin-notebook

item.description:
Alphabet was just named to TIME’s #Time100Companies list 🎉
In the story on Google’s push to the front of the AI race, TIME’s Andrew R. Chow writes: “In 2016, [Sundar Pichai] had declared Google would be an “AI-first company,” and began cultivating a series of projects—custom chips, Cloud, YouTube, and deep AI research—that seemed to have nothing to do with Google’s core search product. All of these bets have paid off, and then some.”
See the full story: https://lnkd.in/eUv9p8te
